That is a sound reason to refuse to assert survival. But nothing in it blocks: AC4, a documentation-only change the brief's own Key interfaces scopes to 'interview-walk.spec.ts: header note only' (verified unchanged in dd3f8f1d..HEAD); AC2, the OPEN unanswered park fixture, which the lane's own report calls 'otherwise straightforward and was not the blocker'; AC3, its fixture-ownership declaration (e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts gained only #879's entry); or the FOCUS-RETURN half of AC1, which is independent of typed-data survival. Nothing was delivered for #897 at all - no commit, no fixture, no header note. Under the riders work order rule 5 and the base order rule 6 ('do every part that does not depend on it, take the most conservative reading for the rest'), the stop is wider than the blocker.

findings.title: The AC4 census does not catch the bypass its own comment says it exists to catch
findings.evidence: tests/select-value-label-census.test.ts's header claims it catches 'an `as any`/`@ts-expect-error` bypass at a `<SelectValue>` call site'. Its childIsFunction() returns true for ANY JsxExpression child that is an Identifier or PropertyAccessExpression, so `<SelectValue>{value}</SelectValue>` - the exact defect shape - is treated as a legitimate function child. CONFIRMED by running the census's own tagNameOf/hasItemsAttribute/childIsFunction logic verbatim (same typescript 5.9.3 resolved from the worktree) against a synthetic source containing a @ts-expect-error'd `<SelectValue>{value}</SelectValue>`: output was 'SelectValue sites: 1 violations flagged: 0'. The census's other two arms (self-closing with no items=, and a direct @base-ui/react/select import outside the wrapper) do work, and its non-vacuity cell (>= 11 sites found) is genuine. So the backstop is real but narrower than advertised - and AC4 asks it to 'fail when a new select renders its value without a label source'.
findings.required_fix: Tighten childIsFunction to accept only ArrowFunction/FunctionExpression children, or resolve an Identifier child to its declaration and require it to be a function; then either the comment's claim becomes true, or the comment is narrowed to what the census actually guarantees.

findings.title: AC3 ('the absence cell cannot pass by luck') is met for cross-cell leaks only; the cell's own reattach timer is unchanged and no detector was added
findings.evidence: lib/clara/use-clara-thread-stop.test.ts:1029-1054 snapshots `const before = net.streams.length` AFTER its own hydration, then spends `absenceSettle(h, 20)` (a fixed macrotask budget) and asserts equality. In that cell `stopReply()` resolves as 'finished', so nothing calls abortStream for its own task - its reattach loop, scheduled by withRunFetch's empty-200 close, is still a real ~1s backoff racing that fixed budget. The two-part fix makes a leak from ANY cell die at the file-level test.afterEach (verified: threadStore.ts:525/530 keep the controller in streamAborts for as long as runClaraTaskStream has not returned, so abortAllStreams can reach it; abortableSleep then resolves synchronously on abort), which is the 'impossible' arm for cross-cell leakage. The 'still detected' arm was not built. Measured green 12/12 isolated + 1 whole-suite by me, 25/25 + 5/5 by the lane, so this is a residual risk, not an observed failure.
findings.required_fix: Accept explicitly on the ticket, or close the last gap cheaply: give this one cell an injected sleepImpl (the runner already accepts one) so its own backoff is deterministic rather than a real 1s timer racing a 20-hop budget.

findings.title: The new mock defines a private POST-body reader instead of the shared readCachedJson, and reads the body before deciding lane ownership
findings.evidence: The base work order (rule 8) says to 'read POST bodies only through the shared readCachedJson (never a private reader)'. e2e/staff-advances-register-mock.mjs:91 defines its own readJson - a verbatim copy of e2e/mock-dispatch.mjs:34's readCachedJson, including the same __e2eParsedBody cache key - and all seven RPC branches call `const body = await readJson(request)` BEFORE the `if (body?.p_client !== SAR.clientId) return false` ownership check, the order mock-dispatch.mjs:50-54's own comment warns against ('call this BEFORE readCachedJson, so a verb this lane does not own returns false without the stream ever being touched'). This is safe today only because the cache key is shared and this hook is dispatched early; it is not safe by construction. House precedent exists - staff-expense-claim-mock.mjs:216 does the identical thing - and the walks all pass (3 + 13 green), so nothing is broken.
findings.required_fix: Import readCachedJson from ./mock-dispatch.mjs and drop the private copy; optionally gate on an owned-verb Set before touching the stream, which is what the shared helper's own comment recommends.

findings.title: SelectValue's useCallback never memoises in practice
findings.evidence: components/ui/select.tsx's resolveChildren is wrapped in React.useCallback with [items, children, placeholder], but almost every call site passes a freshly allocated array literal (e.g. activeAccounts.map(...)), so the dependency changes on every render and the memo never hits. Harmless - the callback is cheap and Base UI re-invokes it per render anyway - but the useCallback buys nothing.

summary: Four clean commits, one ticket each, correct trailers, no migration, no frozen-manifest diff, no blueprint edit, shared files touched minimally at sorted positions. I re-ran every gate: typecheck 0, lint 0, whole apps/web suite 4654 tests / 4652 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped (matching the lane report exactly), frozen-workflows OK, fixture-ownership 20/20, the #1005 batch 46/46, the #956 file 12/12 isolated, streamReattach+invite-mail+threadStore 54/54, and both Playwright lanes green (3 + 13). #1005, #956 and #879 are genuinely delivered and their new cells are non-vacuous by construction. Four things need action before this lands: #897 was stopped whole although three of its four acceptance criteria are independent of the one question that blocked it (blocker); #1005's shipped select.test.tsx header claims per-call-site coverage that does not exist, contradicting the lane's own honest report (major); #1005's AST census has a confirmed blind spot for exactly the @ts-expect-error bypass its comment says it catches (major, reproduced); and #874's AC2 is unmet even at the harness level (major, but arguably superseded by the ticket's own out-of-scope clause - orchestrator's call). The rest are minors: five uncovered Select call sites, items/SelectContent duplication, #875's unstated survey scope and its audit landing nowhere in the repo, the missing .env.example entry, #879's uncovered empty state, and a private POST-body reader where the work order names the shared one.
